title: Stock during a delivery delay
hook: Four units leave daily. A longer lead time changes the reorder arithmetic.

knows: that a model can declare hypothetical quantities
doesNotKnow: Calculate lead-time demand and separate an explicit buffer.

misconception: Delivery lead time has no effect on the quantity consumed before arrival.
objective: Calculate lead-time demand and separate an explicit buffer.

claims.text: Demand is exactly four units/day. Delivery takes three days. A retains an additional eight-unit buffer. Scaled model; constant toy demand; buffer=8; no policy advice.
claims.source: Declared hypothetical inputs and limits in resource-specs.json. No actual product, price, tariff, shelf-life, treatment or physical appliance specification is asserted.

claims.text: The stage's two results are computed by the printed expressions. At Lead-days=3, A=20items and B=12items. The geometry pictures follow the declared dimension relationships; other stage pictures are scaled to the larger displayed comparison and icons are not literal item counts.
claims.source: src/lib/lifehacks/resource-specs.json contains this lesson's numeric AST; src/lib/lifehacks/resource-model.ts evaluates it. A=["+",["*",4,"x"],8]; B=["*",4,"x"]; x denotes Lead-days. At x=3, A=20, B=12; recall at x=6: B=24. Values are fictional/ideal assumptions, not measurements. Display rounds to at most three decimals.

claims.text: Lead-time demand is daily demand multiplied by delivery days. A stated buffer is added separately. Real demand and delays can vary; these values illustrate the distinction, not a universal reorder policy.
claims.source: src/lib/lifehacks/resource-specs.json contains this lesson's numeric AST; src/lib/lifehacks/resource-model.ts evaluates it. A=["+",["*",4,"x"],8]; B=["*",4,"x"]; x denotes Lead-days. The principle follows from those expressions and stated scenario limits.

claims.text: Demand is exactly four units/day. Delivery takes three days. A retains an additional eight-unit buffer. Change only Lead-days to 6. What is B (No-buffer) now? Correct: 24items. Use B's stated rule with Lead-days=6: it gives 24items. Lead-time demand is daily demand multiplied by delivery days. A stated buffer is added separately. Real demand and delays can vary; these values illustrate the distinction, not a universal reorder policy.

recall.question: Demand is exactly four units/day. Delivery takes three days. A retains an additional eight-unit buffer. Change only Lead-days to 6. What is B (No-buffer) now?
recall.why: Use B's stated rule with Lead-days=6: it gives 24items. Lead-time demand is daily demand multiplied by delivery days. A stated buffer is added separately. Real demand and delays can vary; these values illustrate the distinction, not a universal reorder policy.

safety.assumptions: Demand is exactly four units/day. Delivery takes three days. A retains an additional eight-unit buffer.
safety.excluded: No chemical mixtures, medical advice, wiring, safety-device bypass, actual tariffs, financial recommendations, temperature, food-storage or food-safety instructions. All energy powers, durations and tariffs are illustrative.
